title: Request For Expression Of Interest From Tech Hubs And Accelerators To Implement The Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship
summary: The Mastercard Foundation supports new Indigenous-led organizations to advance broadband connectivity in Indigenous communities.
requirements: Hubs must identify and support 36 growth-stage EdTech companies over three years (12 per year).
Hubs must provide holistic support to scale businesses, enhance educational impact/inclusivity, and improve investment readiness/financial sustainability.
Hubs must partner with Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) to train EdTech companies in the science of learning.
Hubs must guide selected EdTech companies in developing market-ready business cases to attract at least 8,000 new end-users (learners) every year for three years.
Hubs must cultivate engagements between EdTech entrepreneurs and key stakeholders, including governments (Ministries of Education and ICT).
Hubs must offer support services such as co-working spaces, design labs, mentorship opportunities, funding avenues, and network access.
duration: Three-year implementation period for hubs; contract begins Q1 2024.
documents: Expression of Interest (EOI) response addressing specified EOI questions (not exceeding five pages, in Microsoft Word format, including a single point of contact).
Completed High-Level Budget reflecting EOI activities (using provided template).
Completed High-Level Organizational Questionnaire and associated attachments (using provided template).
Full program proposals, detailed budget, and detailed organizational questionnaire (required only from the 6 selected finalist hubs at post-selection phase).
benefits: Partnership with Mastercard Foundation Centre for Innovative Teaching and Learning.
Opportunity to serve as a centre of excellence for EdTech products and solutions in Africa.
Co-design process and funding support to deliver fellowship acceleration to 36 EdTech companies over three years.
eligibility: Must be duly incorporated, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of an African jurisdiction.
Must have its principal place of business in Africa.
Must demonstrate a proven record of effectively supporting technology companies in Africa.
Must demonstrate a proven record of working with the Ministry of Education and other stakeholders in promoting EdTech.
Must have a minimum operational experience of at least five years.
Must be African-owned and/or African-led.
Must possess a solid understanding of monitoring and evaluation methodologies, with the ability to collect and analyze data.
howToApply: Submit Expression of Interest response, High-Level Budget, and High-Level Organizational Questionnaire online by August 27, 2023.
Undergo Foundation review and shortlisting (August 28 – September 5, 2023).
Participate in interviews if selected among the 20 shortlisted tech hubs (September 11–22, 2023).
Receive notification if selected as one of six finalist tech hubs (September 25, 2023).
Receive program proposal templates and submit full program proposals (Deadline: October 25, 2023).
Participate in the review and co-design process of full proposals with the Foundation (October 26 – November 30, 2023).
Receive final proposal approval from Mastercard Foundation (December 4, 2023) and start contract (Q1 2024).
selectionProcess: Strategic Alignment (30% weight): Evidence of alignment with Mastercard Foundation values and Strategic Roadmap Briefing Note with a clear plan for outcomes.
Experience (20% weight): Expertise and experience to support program delivery, relevant proposed partnerships, and value-add for partners.
Program Design (20% weight): Clear, coherent design responding to all EOI questions, understanding target group needs, operating context, and diversity/inclusion principles.
Program Implementation (20% weight): Partner capacity to deliver results and satisfaction of Foundation due diligence requirements.
Budget (10% weight): Alignment of budget items with activities, country context, internal expectations, and demonstration of value for money.

summary: The “Monitoring Guidelines” are intended to be a companion document to the “ Supervision Guidelines ”. The goal of the “Monitoring Guidelines” is to provide general recommendations for graduate units on creating structures and processes to support doctoral student success by ensuring that students can make timely progression through their programs. There is likely to be considerable variance in the implementation of some of the recommended procedures, depending, for example, on the nature of the scholarly discipline and the research environment (including the size of graduate unit), or the degree to which research is conducted independently. Graduate units are encouraged to implement the guidelines in a manner appropriate to their discipline and program as well as communicate the relevant procedures in a clear and transparent manner to graduate students and faculty.
